A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same formal-language pre-pretraining study. Their main text, figures, tables, appendix proofs, hyperparameters, and generator code are readable and matchable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pythia training experiments, grammaticality and retrieval evaluations, attention-head pruning, and supplementary analyses in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports a more detailed breakdown of pruning effects across grammatical phenomena in Figure 9.

M1.justification: Formal-language pre-pretraining followed by natural-language training, direct parameter transfer, model architectures, and language generators remain unchanged. The appendix generator is identical apart from formatting.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same formal languages, C4, BLiMP, and verbatim retrieval evaluations. The n-gram metamer datasets and vocabulary-size variants already appear in v1; v2 adds no dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same formal-language comparisons, no-pre-pretraining, C4, random-binary and random-integer controls. The pruning comparison still includes learned, random, and complementary subnetworks.

E3.justification: The methods and Appendix B retain the same models, metrics, budgets, and pruning procedure. However, v2 Figure 6 changes the caption to 1.6B tokens of k-Shuffle Dyck, conflicting with Section 6's 500 steps/30M formal tokens followed by 1.63B C4 tokens. This inconsistency prevents treating the caption as a reliable protocol revision.

E4.justification: v1 Figure 7's grouped morphology-versus-syntax analysis is replaced by v2 Figure 9's phenomenon-level breakdown of pruning effects. The aggregate comparison of pre-pretraining benefits is omitted. The duration sweep, n-gram controls, vocabulary-size analysis, and main pruning experiment remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same error-bar and ± reporting and the pruning result p ≪ 0.001. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or statistical tests are documented.

E6.justification: Table 5's numerical entries and the results plotted in Figures 2–6 are unchanged. v1 Figure 7's aggregate pruning and transfer deltas disappear; v2 Figure 9 newly reports detailed pruning changes, including declines of 12.1 percentage points for subject-verb agreement and 7.6 for irregular forms.

T1.justification: The formal-language definitions, FO(M)/C-RASP characterizations, marginal-rate-of-substitution calculation, and Appendix A lemmas, propositions, and proofs remain substantively identical.

C1.justification: v1 presents the results as supporting both hierarchical structure and C-RASP expressibility. v2 explicitly distinguishes stronger support for hierarchy from only modest support for C-RASP. The transfer, attention-head reuse, and 33% token-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 calls for a larger sample of formal languages to refine the expressivity hypothesis and explicitly identifies benefits beyond 1B parameters and 1.6B tokens as unknown. It drops v1's second-order morphology-benefit discussion and explicit caveat about adverse BLiMP subtask effects, while focusing the mechanistic discussion on individual phenomena.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and explicitly states that the additional analyses use 500 pre-pretraining steps, approximately 30M tokens. Appendix B's hardware, software versions, hyperparameters, and the generator implementation are retained.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning through code-to-language transfer, synthetic-image pretraining, and a contrast with BabyLM curricula, adding works including Petty et al. (2025), Nakamura et al. (2024), and Hu et al. (2024). Some background citations are removed; publication updates to retained works do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, experimental narrative, related work, and discussion undergo extensive rewriting. The numbered contribution summary becomes prose, Sections 5 and 6 receive more descriptive headings, and explanations and qualifications are integrated throughout the narrative.

P2.justification: The aggregate bar chart in v1 Figure 7 is replaced by the appendix heatmap in v2 Figure 9. Existing figures are renumbered or repositioned, Table 5 moves to a separate appendix page, and Code 1 becomes Figure 10. Captions expand, while most displays retain their design.

improvement.justification: v2 better aligns the central expressivity claim with Table 5's unchanged evidence: k-Dyck and k-Shuffle Dyck perform similarly on language modeling and grammaticality, with clearer separation on retrieval. The detailed pruning breakdown and code-access information improve transparency. These gains outweigh limited drawbacks, including the misleading Figure 6 token-budget caption and removal of the explicit caveat about BLiMP subtask regressions.
